bricks.label: struct AVLNode
bricks.plain_english: Defines an AVL node — stores a value, left and right pointers, and a height field used for balancing.
bricks.scene_description: A single sphere appears with a height label beside it.

bricks.label: height()
bricks.plain_english: Returns a node's height, or 0 for NULL. Used by all rotation logic — every rotation decision depends on this.
bricks.scene_description: Height numbers appear beside each node.

bricks.label: getBalance()
bricks.plain_english: Returns height(left) - height(right). Positive means left-heavy, negative means right-heavy. If |balance| > 1, a rotation is needed.
bricks.scene_description: Balance factor labels appear beside each node. Labels turn red when |bf| > 1.

bricks.label: createNode()
bricks.plain_english: Allocates an AVL node with height 1 — a new leaf always starts at height 1.
bricks.scene_description: New sphere spawns with height label 1.

bricks.label: rightRotate()
bricks.plain_english: Rotates right around a node. The left child becomes the new root of this subtree. Fixes left-heavy imbalance.
bricks.scene_description: Rotation animation — nodes pivot rightward around the imbalanced node.

bricks.label: leftRotate()
bricks.plain_english: Rotates left around a node. The right child becomes the new root. Fixes right-heavy imbalance.
bricks.scene_description: Mirror rotation animation — nodes pivot leftward.

bricks.label: insert()
bricks.plain_english: BST insert plus rebalancing. After each insert, walks back up checking balance factors. Rotates where needed.
code_snippet: struct AVLNode* insert(struct AVLNode* root, int value) {
else if (value > root->data) root->right = insert(root->right, value);
if (bal > 1 && value > root->left->data)  { root->left = leftRotate(root->left);  return rightRotate(root); }
if (bal < -1 && value < root->right->data) { root->right = rightRotate(root->right); return leftRotate(root); }
bricks.scene_description: Node inserts, then balance factors update. A rotation fires if the tree becomes unbalanced.

bricks.label: inorder()
bricks.plain_english: In-order traversal showing balance factors beside each value.
bricks.scene_description: Nodes light up in sorted order. Balance factors pulse beside each one.
